speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific characteristics of your headache, such as its location, intensity, and whether it is associated with nausea or visual changes like halos.

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To help narrow down the cause, is your headache located strictly behind one eye, and do you notice any physical changes in your eye, such as a reddish halo around the vision or pain when pressing on your eye?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bilateral Orbital Pseudotumor (Idiopathic Orbital Inflammation).

Given your age, the unilateral or bilateral nature of the pain behind the eye, and the concurrent worsening vision without systemic signs of infection or malignancy, this clinical picture strongly suggests orbital pseudotumor. I am requesting a CT scan of the orbits with contrast to confirm the presence of orbital tissue inflammation and rule out other masses. REQUEST IMAGES: Orbital_CT_with_contrast.
